content:
Plan: docs/phases/atomic-turn-slot-marker.md (commit 9660c4f on branch phase-80-atomic-turn-slot-marker; roadmap Phase 80 entry in the same commit).

What: the turn slot marker (.tagteam/turns/inflight.json) is written with Path.write_text (truncate, then write) by claim_turn_slot() and update_turn_slot(), while read_inflight() is lock-free. A reader between truncate and write sees an empty file, gets None, and the held slot reads as free. Proposed fix: one private helper in headless.py writes a temp file in turns/ and os.replace()s it over the marker; both writers use it. Readers unchanged.

This is the root cause of the launchpad endpoint test flake (CI on main 2026-09-25 run 36201554429 and 2026-11-16): test_watch_session_and_launch_endpoints fails at assert conv['slot']['held'] while the turn row says running. The rewrite readers meet is update_turn_slot() from on_spawn, just after a turn starts.

Verified before writing the plan (nothing committed besides docs):
- Direct measurement: one thread looping update_turn_slot(), one looping slot_status(), 5 s: 20 of 580 reads said free while held.
- The CI failure reproduced with the identical assertion, 3 of 3, using a scratch pytest plugin that slows the real Path.write_text on marker files (truncate, 1 s, write) and delays the server's slot read 0.4 s. Unmodified, the test passed 5 of 5 locally.
- Checked writers: only claim_turn_slot and update_turn_slot write the marker; briefer.py and controls.py read or unlink.
Not verified: behaviour on Windows (os.replace over an open file); the plan proposes a short bounded retry on PermissionError and I have no Windows run for it.

Questions for review: (1) is a bounded retry on PermissionError the right Windows handling, or should update_turn_slot just return False there; (2) write_pidfile() has the same shape and is left out of scope with a backlog entry: agree, or fold it in; (3) are the two deterministic tests (marker is whole just before the replace; failed replace leaves the old marker and no temp file) enough to pin this, with the two-thread run as supporting evidence only.

Approved. Reviewed docs/phases/atomic-turn-slot-marker.md at 9660c4f against claim_turn_slot(), update_turn_slot(), read_inflight(), and slot_status(). Both writes currently truncate the published marker while readers are lock-free; same-directory temporary write followed by replacement addresses that window while preserving the writer lock, ownership checks, and reader behavior. Scope and success criteria are appropriate.

Answers to the review questions:
1. A short bounded PermissionError retry is reasonable. Keep it narrowly scoped to the replacement operation (and Windows if intended only for Windows), propagate exhaustion so update returns False and claim raises, and do not retry unrelated OSError failures. Add deterministic coverage for transient failure followed by success and exhausted retries; simulated failures do not establish Windows compatibility, so retain that qualification without a Windows run.
2. Keep write_pidfile out of this phase; the separate backlog entry is sufficient.
3. The before-replace observation and failed-replace preservation tests are the right primary regression checks. Along with the planned failed-claim and cleanup checks, they cover the intended behavior. Also inject a temporary-file write failure to exercise cleanup before replacement. Keep the threaded run as supporting evidence only, as proposed.

Minor implementation pointers: existing slot ownership tests are in tests/test_lead_chat.py rather than tests/test_headless.py; either location for the new focused tests is acceptable. prune_turn_logs currently collects all regular files except inflight.json, so a .tmp suffix alone does not make a temporary file invisible to pruning; avoid a claim that it does. That does not block atomic publication or require a pruning redesign here.

No tests run for this plan review. Proceed to implementation and use the gate for the one full-suite run.
